implication: A Regulation 31(4) disclosure marks the point at which an acquirer has crossed into mandatory open-offer territory under the Takeover Code; the acquirer's identity, quantum acquired, and cumulative holding will determine whether a full Regulation 26 open offer becomes obligatory.

Open-offer rules; acquirer must make a general offer to shareholders at minimum price if acquisition threshold (typically 25% of voting capital) is breached.

headline: IMFAL Discloses Substantial Share Acquisition Under SEBI Takeover Regulations
sum: Indian Metals & Ferro Alloys Limited filed a Regulation 31(4) disclosure with NSE, signalling a substantial acquisition of shares triggering mandatory takeover code scrutiny.
detail: IMFAL submitted its formal disclosure to NSE under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. This regulation requires disclosure once an acquirer's voting rights reach or exceed thresholds (typically 25%, or crossing defined slab limits). The disclosure itself triggers a 4-trading-day window during which the acquirer may not deal further in the target's securities, and a 30-calendar-day clock begins for any mandatory open offer. The identity of the acquirer, the shares acquired, and the consideration remain to be corroborated from the full disclosure document.
